title: Story unlock beats re-show once for existing profiles: seen-key rename orphans old board-unlock-generic keys

title: Build placement in lockstep resolves from the LOCAL mouse; raw canvas click confirms builds entirely outside the intent stream
claim: In multiplayer, building placement desyncs deterministically: (a) BuildSystem registers a raw canvas 'click' listener (BuildSystem.ts:392) whose handler onCanvasClick (BuildSystem.ts:1003-1005) calls this.confirm(this.currentAt) directly — a local DOM click that spends gold and places a building on ONE client only, never entering the lockstep input stream; (b) even the lockstep-routed confirm (LockstepInput.confirm → Game.confirmAction, Game.ts:4191 → buildSystem.confirm, BuildSystem.ts:599-602) resolves the ghost position via updateGhostPosition (BuildSystem.ts:1007-1026), which raycasts the client's own pointerClientX/Y through its own camera whenever pointerReady is true (set permanently by the first local pointermove). Two clients executing the same confirm intent at the same tick place the building at different coordinates. Buildings and economy.gold are both in the state hash (Game.ts:1590-1608), so any mouse-driven build in mp trips a desync.
evidence: BuildSystem.ts:391-392 `this.canvas.addEventListener('pointermove', this.onPointerMove); this.canvas.addEventListener('click', this.onCanvasClick);` — BuildSystem.ts:1003-1005 `private readonly onCanvasClick = (): void => { this.confirm(this.currentAt); };` — BuildSystem.ts:1008-1016 ghost position from `this.pointerClientX/Y` raycast against `this.camera`. The mp integration (Game.ts:1488-1502) never disables or de-pointers the build path the way it did for blast aim (Game.ts:3958 forces auto blast aim when multiplayerActive()).
fix_sketch: When multiplayerActive(): ignore onCanvasClick and force the keyboard/hero-relative ghost fallback (pointerReady=false path anchors to actionActorPosition, which is deterministic), or add a quantized ghost-position/aim field to LockstepInput and drive updateGhostPosition from the intent stream.

title: Level-up picks, HUD buttons, death-overlay buttons and baron-ceremony skip mutate the sim locally while lockstep ticks keep being consumed
claim: A whole family of DOM-driven inputs bypasses the lockstep intent stream and mutates sim state on one client only. Worst case: every level-up in mp guarantees a desync — handleUpgradeIntent (Game.ts:3528-3532) applies progression.applyUpgrade from a local overlay click; each player picks their own upgrade at their own wall-clock time, and progression.stacks is hashed (Game.ts:1583). Same class: handleUiIntent 'pause'/'restart'/'toggle_build_menu'/'select_buildable' (Game.ts:3500-3521), DeathOverlay 'Try Again' → resetRun (Game.ts:838), RunManager secured-choice buttons, and skipBaronCeremony bound to raw window pointerdown/keydown (Game.ts:796-797, 2880). The amplifier is that mpClient.pump() consumes a tick unconditionally at Game.ts:1289 before any pause/overlay gating, so a client that is locally paused (or still in ceremony/levelup) consumes ticks WITHOUT simulating them while the peer simulates those same ticks — the two clients execute different numbers of sim steps and hard-desync.
evidence: Game.ts:1289 `const lockstepTick = this.mpClient?.pump(...)` runs before the state checks; sim block gated at Game.ts:1359 `if (this.state.simActive ...)`; GameState.simActive is `playing && !paused` (GameState.ts:22-24). handleUpgradeIntent Game.ts:3528-3532 `const picked = this.progression.offer?.[intent.index]; if (picked) this.progression.applyUpgrade(picked.id);` — click-only, no lockstep routing. skipBaronCeremony registered at Game.ts:796-797 on window; ceremony early-return path Game.ts:1302-1310 skips the whole sim while ticks are consumed.
fix_sketch: In mp mode, route every sim-mutating UI intent through the LockstepInput stream (extend it with pickUpgradeIndex, uiPause, uiRestart, selectBuildable, skipCeremony), or freeze tick consumption (stop pumping) while any locally-gated overlay/pause is active on any client via a relay-coordinated pause.

title: Roster changes are applied at websocket-message arrival, not tick-aligned — any mid-run join attempt or leave desyncs the running pair
claim: LockstepClient.handle applies 'joined'/'roster' messages to this.roster immediately on arrival (LockstepClient.ts:202-211). Game.syncMultiplayerActors (Game.ts:1673) reads that roster inside consumeMultiplayerTick and creates Hero actors, flips visibility, and calls actor.resetRun(spawn) whenever playerId/slot changes — all sim-relevant (visibleActorPositions feeds enemy targeting, harvest, gold pickups; actor hp/pos are hashed at Game.ts:1578-1585). Because clients consume buffered ticks at different depths, the same roster message lands at DIFFERENT sim ticks on each client, so actors appear/disappear/respawn at different ticks → divergent enemy targeting → desync. The relay makes this reachable: MultiplayerRoom.join has no 'game started' gate (functions/api/_multiplayer.ts:168-199), so a late joiner broadcasts roster(3) to the running pair before being kicked by the bad_tick check (functions/api/_multiplayer.ts:217-219 → socket closed at 154). Even that doomed join attempt spawns-then-hides a third actor at unaligned ticks on the two survivors.
evidence: LockstepClient.ts:209-211 `if (message.type === 'roster') { this.roster = normalizeRoster(message.players); return; }` — no tick stamping. Game.ts syncMultiplayerActors: `if (!previous || previous.playerId !== player.playerId || previous.slot !== slot) { actor.resetRun(this.multiplayerSpawnPosition(slot, roster.length)); }` and actor creation loop `while (this.actors.length < roster.length)`. functions/api/_multiplayer.ts:173 only checks `this.players.size >= MAX_PLAYERS`.
fix_sketch: Tick-stamp roster transitions: relay includes an effectiveTick (>= nextFlushTick + delay) in roster broadcasts and clients defer applying the change until consuming that tick; reject joins after nextFlushTick > 0 at the relay so a doomed join never reaches the roster broadcast.

title: Desync recovery cannot converge: snapshot tick is ignored, nextSimTick is never rewound, and detection is one-sided under skew
claim: The recovery protocol restores identical STATE but not identical TIME. (1) On 'snapshot', LockstepClient.handle (LockstepClient.ts:226-232) passes only message.snapshot to onSnapshot and, on success, just unpauses — this.nextSimTick, nextInputTick, and the bundles map are untouched, and the relay never replays bundles from the snapshot tick. Clients pause at whatever tick they were on when the peer hash arrived (async to consumption), so client A can resume applying input bundle 310 while client B resumes at 305 against the SAME restored state → immediate re-divergence → desync loop (each loop shows the 'The wire crossed' card again). (2) Detection is one-sided under skew: handle 'hash' (LockstepClient.ts:222-223) drops the peer hash when the local hash for that tick isn't computed yet (`if (local && ...)`), so a lagging client never detects; only the leading client pauses and restores while the other keeps its diverged state — if the restored latestSnapshot came from the non-restoring client's own diverged push, the pair never converges.
evidence: LockstepClient.ts:226-232 `if (message.type === 'snapshot') { if (this.options.onSnapshot?.(message.snapshot)) { this.paused = false; this.resyncs += 1; } }` — no use of message.tick, no counter reset. desync() at 236-242 sets paused (pump then also stops SENDING inputs at 139-144, stalling the relay flush for the peer). Game.restoreMultiplayerRunSuspendSnapshot (Game.ts:1538-1544) likewise never touches the client tick counters. Relay stores only latestSnapshot from whichever client pushed last (functions/api/_multiplayer.ts:258-266).
fix_sketch: Make recovery two-phase and tick-aligned: both clients pause via a relay-coordinated 'resync at tick T' message, restore the snapshot tagged with its capture tick, set nextSimTick = snapshotTick + 1, and have the relay rebroadcast (or clients re-request) input bundles from snapshotTick+1; compare hashes only when both sides have reported the tick (buffer unmatched peer hashes instead of dropping them).

Severity: high — the shipped recovery mechanism for a player-facing co-op mode structurally cannot do its job under realistic network timing and can amplify failures, with no escape short of quitting.

Severity calibration: high — the recovery safety net of the new player-reachable MP mode structurally fails under any real network latency and violates the determinism law (message arrival timing decides which input ticks feed the sim); not critical since it is MP-only, post-desync only, with no default-path or save impact.
